title: Web startup comparison
lead: Compare startup behavior under disclosed playback conditions and inspect individual outcomes before reading a summary.

blocks.caption: Comparison conditions with Configuration candidates expanded.

blocks.text: Choose a player or All players, then choose SDK import mode, settings and trials per player. Each trial records the SDK version. Both resolutions use a fixed-quality HLS rendition and the same en-labelled audio track.

rows: SDK import: On selection
Import and evaluate the SDK after the accepted content selection; this time is included in selection-based timings.
SDK import: Before selection
Import only the SDK before selecting content. Player creation and media loading still belong to the trial.
Common conditions + SDK defaults
Keep the common playback conditions while retaining vendor defaults for other settings.
Common conditions + startup settings
Use the documented startup settings. Open Configuration candidates to change the hls.js worker or Shaka segment prefetch limit. The Web X playback policy remains Data (2).

blocks.text: SDK import mode does not establish a cold or warm HTTP cache. The public screen uses browser-managed caching. Keep browser, network, resolution and import mode consistent when comparing results.

items: Choose the player, SDK import mode, settings and Trials per player. Wait until the content buttons become available.
Select Compare this video on the required resolution. Trials run one at a time, each with a fresh video document.
Keep the tab in the foreground. Stop or moving the page to the background cancels the run, including preparation between trials. Completed results remain available.

blocks.text: Playback starts muted, from the beginning, at normal speed. A successful trial requires the adapter’s start operation to complete, a native playing event and advancing media. Moving frames are also checked when video-frame callbacks are supported. SDK Ready alone is insufficient.

For automatic evaluation, choose All players, Common conditions + startup settings and at least six trials per player, then select Evaluate candidates and compare on a content card. The app evaluates the hls.js worker values true/false and Shaka prefetch limits 0/1/2; Web X keeps Data (2). It selects each player’s candidate using the median Selection → Playing time, then runs new confirmation trials with those settings fixed.

Candidate evaluation and confirmation are separate phases. Both remain in the individual records and JSON, while the current summary uses confirmation only. Incomplete screening or no fully successful candidate keeps that player’s explicit fallback: hls.js worker enabled, Shaka prefetch 0 or Web X Data (2), with a reason. A selected candidate is not a proven optimum.

When all players are selected, trials are interleaved in balanced blocks. The recorded seed determines the order; the order changes between runs. This avoids always giving the same player the first position without running players concurrently.

blocks.caption: Summary and individual outcomes after one playback per player. The screen does not display a ranking because this run has too few trials.

rows: Playing from selection
Accepted content selection to the video element’s playing event. This includes SDK import after selection when that mode is used.
Playback startup (Play → Playing)
Video startup time (VST) is defined here as the app’s play request to native video playing. It differs from Bitmovin Analytics VIDEO_STARTUPTIME.
First frame callback
Selection to entry into the first video-frame callback. This is the callback-observation time, not compositor submission or physical-display time.
Play → moving frame
Play request to a later frame callback whose media time has advanced. Read it separately from the first paused frame.
SDK Ready / SDK Playing
Vendor events with their original names and meanings. They are not interchangeable across players.
Missing or failed observations
Read the status and reason. An unavailable observation remains missing; it is not a zero-millisecond success.

blocks.text: Groups keep player version, content, SDK import mode, settings, cache condition and explicit tuning values separate. n counts successful trials with a valid value for the selected metric. Failure, cancellation and missing counts remain visible; a trial can be both failed and missing a metric.

Median describes the middle of the successful values. p95 uses the nearest-rank method: sort the values and take rank ceil(0.95 × n). With few trials, p95 can equal the maximum. Read n and the outcome counts alongside both statistics.

A smallest-median label requires matching conditions and versions, all players, equal successful sample counts of at least five per player, and no failures, cancellations or missing values for that metric. Exact ties stay ties. The label applies to that cohort, not every stream, device or network.

Select Save JSON before leaving the page to retain conditions (safe content identifiers and settings), sequence seeds, phases, outcomes and observations. Export schema 2 adds device-clock timestamps in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time): exportedAt is the save time; each trial's measuredAt is its start time. Each trial keeps its startup browser family and major version, OS family, reported logical processors, optional approximate memory in GiB, viewport size in CSS pixels and pixel ratio. Browser and OS families are coarse user-agent classifications, not verified platform or playback-engine observations. Processor counts may be reduced and memory is approximate; neither measures CPU utilization or player/process memory. Unknown values are null with a reason, and later resizing does not alter earlier records. The export excludes raw user-agent text, device models, hostnames, license and API keys, source URLs, headers, raw SDK errors and SDK metadata. Clear results removes the displayed records.

items: If the browser rejects play or the Player license/domain is invalid, retain the failure and check the reason before repeating. Player Web X uses the existing Web license setup.
If first-frame timing is unavailable, check browser support. Playing or loadeddata is not used to fabricate a frame timestamp.
If no smallest-median label appears, check outcome counts and comparison conditions. A single trial is useful for inspecting behavior, but does not meet the comparison sample requirement.
